chunks: You will see the wicked on that day bound together in chains.

key_terms.يَوْمَئِذٍ: On that day (referring to the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the state of criminals on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Ibrahim (14:49) is often linked with the concept of *al-asfad* (shackles) as a physical manifestation of the sins that bound the soul during life, emphasizing the inescapability of divine justice. The imagery serves as a stark contrast to the freedom of the righteous, illustrating how the *mujrimun* are not merely imprisoned but are actively presented before God with their deeds attached to their necks. This scene underscores the reality of the Hereafter (*Akhirah*) as a place where spiritual states become tangible physical realities.
